mechaber/1:main: Laws of eating the afikoman. Containing 2 seifim: After finishing the entire meal, each one eats a kezayit from the guarded matza under the cloth, in commemoration of the Pesach offering eaten on a full stomach; and he eats it while leaning; and he does not bless on it; and he should be careful to eat it before chatzot. {Rama: And he should prepare himself that Hallel too be recited before chatzot (Ran chapter Afikoman and seif 2 of Megillah}.}
mechaber/2:main: If one forgot and did not eat afikoman and did not remember until he washed his hands or said 'let us bless,' he eats afikoman without the blessing of HaMotzi. And if he did not remember until he blessed Birkas Hamazon — if he remembered before he blessed borei peri hagafen, he washes his hands and blesses HaMotzi and eats the afikoman {Rama: and he returns and blesses Birkas Hamazon and blesses borei peri hagafen and drinks the cup (Beit Yosef)}. And if he did not remember until after he blessed borei peri hagafen, he does not eat afikoman and relies on matza he ate during the meal, for all are guarded from the time of kneading. But in a place where they are accustomed to guard matza of mitzvah from the time of reaping — even if he did not remember until after Hallel, he washes his hands and blesses HaMotzi and eats afikoman. {Rama: And he returns and blesses on the cup, and one need not be concerned that he adds to the cups (responsa of Rosh general rule 24). And if the afikoman was lost, he eats one kezayit from another guarded matza (Rokeach}.}
baer-heitev/1:_: tiny bit. And the latter agree that from the beginning one should eat about 2 olives, 1 male for Passover and 1 male for the matzah that is eaten with it, and at the very least no small amount of matzot. And the apothecary, you shall not have eating afikoman for Tirha and Esi' 15 in the Haga that it should not be eaten for coarse eating Da'a3 that Passover is eaten on the fasting person MM in that he may desire to eat in 28 20 of the the Master I saw the sons of Alyah who were kissing the unleavened bread and the moror and also a sukkah when entering and leaving, as well as 4 species that are in love and everything for the mitzvah, and blessed is he who worships the Omnipresent with joy. And in the name of the Rabbinate in the name of the Rashel and on Pesach, Mauveen Siman 15 wrote another verse and the customs of taking a stick in my hand and my shoes on my feet and saying this is how you eat it with your shoes strapped [on your feet] and your stick in your hand and you ate it in haste. this:
baer-heitev/2:א: (א) He does not eat. Acharonim agreed that now too he eats afikoman and blesses Birkas Hamazon without a cup (Magen Avraham); see Netziv.
baer-heitev/2:ב: (ב) Reaping. Meaning matza of mitzvah they guard from reaping, not other matzot; and he does not eat from that matza during the meal.
baer-heitev/2:ג: (ג) That he adds. If he remembers after Hallel he returns and says Hallel on the cup; if he did not remember until drinking the third cup he blesses Birkas Hamazon between third and fourth and does not return to drink the third cup (Magen Avraham, Chok Yaakov, Taz). Custom to break a piece from afikoman, pierce it, and hang it; no prohibition concern in piercing on Yom Tov (Magen Avraham siman 500 seif 7).
beer-hagolah/1:א: (א) Rif and Rosh in end of chapter Afikoman, and Rambam.
beer-hagolah/1:ב: (ב) I cited it above siman 472 seif 7.
beer-hagolah/1:ג: (ג) Statement of Rava according to Rav Acha bar Yaakov 120; Rosh wrote correct to be stringent — end of first chapter.
beer-hagolah/2:א: (א) Tur in name of R' Peretz and Hagahot Maimoniyot in name of Semak.
beer-hagolah/2:ב: (ב) There in name of Avi Ezri, etc.
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (c) As an olive tree, it is called a “sea” and in a ridge that brought me from the mountain to another taste:
machatzit-hashekel/2:א: (א) Without a blessing — as explained, etc., meaning we hold siman 479 that even if he only said 'let us bless' and did not say the full formula, if he wishes to eat he must bless; nevertheless there it is written seif 2 that a guest accustomed to the host's table — even if he said 'let us bless' it is not distraction; and similarly on Passover night as the Merciful One established, etc. — even if he said 'let us bless' it is not distraction. However there in siman 479 it is not written regarding a guest that saying 'let us bless' is not distraction, only when he said it; but if he washed hands it is not clear there; and it implies even for a guest it is distraction; and here even if he washed he need not bless — one may say the reason per Magen Avraham there seif gimmel: if at the time of saying 'let us bless' he clearly distracted himself, even a guest is distraction; therefore when washing it is clear distraction.
machatzit-hashekel/2:ב: (2) Masha'k is merciful in every matter, lest he be distracted. Dain depends on his mind that he should fulfill the Omnipresent's commandments, and certainly the forgetfulness caused him to take his hands and not to be completely distracted:
machatzit-hashekel/2:ג: (ג) Bach wrote in name of Rashal he should not eat it; this is Beit Yosef's view. Bach wrote the reason: if he remembered after Birkas Hamazon and has not yet blessed borei peri hagafen, one should not act as Mechaber wrote — not bless on the cup, wash hands, bless HaMotzi, etc. — for originally they enacted generally to bless borei peri hagafen on the third cup after Birkas Hamazon even if eating not finished, since blessing on food is stated generally; if he blesses on the cup and after eating afikoman blesses Birkas Hamazon again on a cup he adds cups; so too even at 'let us bless' he should not eat afikoman, for some hold siman 479 that even at 'let us bless' it is forbidden to eat again even if wishing to bless HaMotzi until first Birkas Hamazon on what already eaten — if he does so he must again come to Birkas Hamazon; therefore better not eat afikoman and rely on matza eaten during meal, though we do not hold so at 'let us bless' as above siman 479 — nevertheless why enter ourselves into dispute of poskim — end.
magen-avraham/1:_: Kezayit. Maharil wrote l'chatchila one should take two olives: one in commemoration of Pesach and one in commemoration of matza eaten with it; and at minimum one should not reduce below a kezayit (Darkei Moshe, Bach).
magen-avraham/2:א: (א) Without a blessing. For we rely on divine mercy regarding afikoman (siman 479), and Bach wrote in the name of Rashal that one should not bless on it.
magen-avraham/2:ב: (ב) He washes his hands. Since he blessed borei peri hagafen his mind was diverted, as written siman 479.
magen-avraham/2:ג: (ג) He does not eat afikoman. For if he eats he must take another cup for Birkas Hamazon and it is like adding to the cups; nevertheless Rashi, Rivan, Rashba, and Raavad wrote he eats a kezayit and blesses without a cup — end; and it appears to me one who is not careful all year and sometimes blesses without a cup may now too eat afikoman and bless without a cup (siman 482); and similarly Semak wrote one not careful all year regarding third meal on Shabbat when it falls on erev Pesach should not eat.
magen-avraham/2:ד: (ד) He relies on matza. Even though he ate other things afterward, he fulfills b'dieved.
magen-avraham/2:ה: (ה) Guarding matza of mitzvah. And he does not eat from that matza during the meal.
magen-avraham/2:ו: (ו) After Hallel. It appears he should return and say Hallel on the cup; and if he did not remember until he drank the third cup, he blesses borei peri hagafen between third and fourth and returns and drinks the third cup.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) Kezayit — and l'chatchila it is good to take two olives: one in commemoration of Pesach and one in commemoration of matza eaten with it.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) (b) Everyone, and no women owe it:
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (ג) On a full stomach — see above siman 476 seif 1 in Hagahah and what we wrote there in Mishna Berurah.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (ד) He eats it leaning — b'dieved if he forgot and ate without leaning he need not return and eat if eating is difficult for him.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (5) (e) And he will not bless him - which is only in remembrance, and as above he wrote that the Omnipresent saw the sons of Alyah who were kissing the unleavened bread and the moror, as well as the sukkah when entering and leaving, as well as four species that are in love and all for the love of the mitzvah. And blessed is he who worships the Omnipresent with joy:
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (ו) And he should be careful, etc. — since it is remembrance of Pesach he must eat it in Pesach's time, and Pesach is eaten only until midnight — and all the more the first olive on which we bless for eating matzah — he must be very careful not to delay until midnight; and b'dieved if delayed, Rishonim are uncertain if he fulfilled; therefore he should eat it and not bless on eating matzah; and maror too, although d'rabbanan, he should be careful to eat before midnight, and if delayed eat without blessing; and if it darkened for him before Haggadah until near midnight — he should sanctify and drink the first cup and wash hands and bless motzi and on eating matzah and eat, and also bless on maror immediately before midnight, and afterward say Haggadah and afterward continue his meal [Acharonim].
mishnah-berurah/1:ז: (ז) That Hallel too — meaning with its blessing he blesses afterward, he should say it l'chatchila before chatzot.
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (1) (h) Without the blessing of the issuer - Daf Dabsiman Ket 11 11 Dam said Habel len and be blessed, O he is distracted, and if he wants to eat, he should go back and bless Haka Atka, Darhamna Samkinan Dain, it depends on his mind, that he should fulfill the will of the Omnipresent, and surely the forgetfulness caused him to take his hands or say Habel belen, and be blessed, and not be completely distracted:
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (ב) (ט) He washes hands — since he blessed Birkas Hamazon he diverted attention; see Peri Megadim who wrote wash without blessing, especially when he knows he did not divert — lest he bless in vain.
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (ג) (י) And he blesses borei peri hagafen, etc. — this is the third cup; they did not require drinking this cup adjacent to the first Birkas Hamazon, for they only enacted the third cup at the end of eating; and this case where he forgot to eat afikoman is as one who did not finish his eating (Bach).
mishnah-berurah/2:ד: (ד) (יא) He does not eat afikoman — for if he eats he must bless Birkas Hamazon, and Birkas Hamazon requires a cup, and then it is like adding cups; Acharonim wrote this is for poskim who hold siman 484 that Birkas Hamazon requires a cup; but per our custom as those who hold Birkas Hamazon ordinarily does not require a cup — now too he eats afikoman and blesses Birkas Hamazon without a cup.
mishnah-berurah/2:ה: (ה) (יב) He relies on matza, etc. — meaning this will be considered for afikoman even though he did not intend then for that purpose; and although we hold siman 479 that after afikoman one may not eat anything, and he ate other things after the matza — nevertheless b'dieved he fulfilled.
mishnah-berurah/2:ו: (ו) (יג) During the meal, etc. — for if he had no guarded matza at all during the meal, even if at the start of the meal he ate a kezayit of guarded matza properly, he returns and eats afikoman, for he did not fulfill the mitzvah of afikoman with that, since we require it eaten on a full stomach (Peri Chadash, Peri Megadim).
mishnah-berurah/2:ז: (ז) (יד) Guarding matza of mitzvah — and he did not eat from that matza during the meal so he could rely on it for afikoman.
mishnah-berurah/2:ח: (ח) (טו) Even if he did not remember, etc. — and all the more so if he remembered before beginning Hallel he certainly eats afikoman and blesses Birkas Hamazon on the cup; there is no concern of drinking between third and fourth cup which is forbidden as below siman 479, since the third was in error and the cup he now blesses on becomes the third.
mishnah-berurah/2:ט: (ט) To the other hand, the psalmist, and also greeted him on the fourth cup that followed him:
mishnah-berurah/2:י: (י) (יז) One need not be concerned, etc. — since initially the third cup was in error, this cup is considered the third cup; and even though he preceded the Hallel cup which should be last, order does not impede. Know that per our custom all year to bless Birkas Hamazon without a cup, here too he eats afikoman without a cup.
turei-zahav/1:_: A kezayit for each. Maharil wrote one must eat measure of two olives, i.e. like a chicken egg, for it is dearer than other mitzvot whose measure is kezayit which is half an egg; if cannot eat all that nevertheless not less than kezayit — end.
turei-zahav/2:א: (א) From reaping. Meaning matza of mitzvah they guard from reaping, not other matzot — therefore one does not fulfill with them where there is matza of mitzvah.
turei-zahav/2:ב: (ב) One need not be concerned, etc. — since the third was in error, the cup he now blesses on becomes the third; if he remembered after blessing on Hallel which should be last, order of blessings does not impede.
